_comment: ACCEPTANCE GATE for the Rust Ion layer. Numbers measured on <host> (<internal-ip>) 2026-07-31 from the reference implementation at <reference-repo>, and independently reproduced by a second agent (441.4x vs 444.4x on the showcase case - run-to-run variance, not disagreement). The Rust port must clear the floor on the speedup column and MUST NOT EXCEED the correctness column. Nothing here was typed from memory.

source.language: Python (algorithm reference only, NOT the product)

correctness_gate.policy: No timing number may be printed for an operator that has not first matched dense numpy to <1e-9. Adopted verbatim from the reference implementation. A speed number attached to a wrong answer is a lie.

speedup_gate._note: n=4096 matvec unless stated. Speedup vs numpy dense @ on the same machine.
speedup_gate._scheme: Rewritten 2026-08-01 per reports/ion-gate-target-semantics-2026-08-01.md, which also carries the full argument for why this replaces the single-band scheme rather than just widening it. Each case below carries TWO independently-provenanced target kinds instead of one cross-hardware band: 'floor' (the reference implementation's ratio on <host>, kept as a hard lower bound our Rust port must never fall below -- a Rust port being slower than the Python original it reimplements is a genuine regression) and 'reproduction' (a [0.5x, 2.0x] band recorded ON THIS MACHINE FROM THIS IMPLEMENTATION by `bench --record-reproduction`, so a future run that halves our own speedup is still caught even though it can never be caught by comparing against <host>'s numbers). A case passes only if it clears its floor AND sits inside its reproduction band. Band-checking a Rust-on-M4/Accelerate measurement against a Python-on-<host> ratio was the category error being fixed here; reproduction.recorded=false means `bench --record-reproduction` has not been run since this schema was introduced -- the gate cannot band-check what has never been measured on this machine, and correctly refuses to pass until it has.

baseline_competitiveness_gate._comment: Added 2026-08-01 per reports/ion-gate-baseline-audit-2026-08-01.md. Every speedup above is only meaningful if our Rust dense baseline (ionp-ion/src/baseline.rs) is itself competitive with what a numpy user would actually run -- otherwise the ratio is inflated by however slow our baseline is, not by anything Ion did. bench.rs shells out to the canonical numpy/BLAS reference (see 'source' block below) at RUN TIME, on the same op/dtype/n, and compares wall time to the Rust baseline it just measured. There is no committed numpy-timing number here on purpose: a frozen number would go stale on different hardware or after a numpy/BLAS upgrade and could certify a baseline that is no longer fair. See ionp-ion/src/numpy_ref.rs for the implementation and the fuller justification.
baseline_competitiveness_gate.policy: If rust_baseline_seconds / numpy_seconds > threshold_mult, the case is INFLATED_BASELINE: bench.rs must suppress the headline speedup ratio for that case entirely (not print a ratio derived from a baseline known to be unfair) and fail the overall gate. A numpy measurement that cannot be obtained (canonical interpreter missing, bad output, etc) is treated the same as INFLATED_BASELINE -- unverified competitiveness is not fair competitiveness. `bench --record-reproduction` additionally refuses to write a new reproduction band for any case whose baseline is not FAIR this run: recording a band from an inflated baseline would bake the inflation into the future gate.

audit_finding_same_machine_2026_08_01.note: rust baseline was 2.07x slower than numpy BLAS on identical complex input, and the benchmark was additionally paying a 3.78x dtype tax by running Complex64 over real-valued standard_normal data. These are historical audit numbers for context only -- bench.rs re-measures both the baseline and the numpy comparator fresh on every run; nothing here is read by the gate at run time.

dtype_honesty_gate._comment: Added 2026-08-01 per reports/ion-gate-baseline-audit-2026-08-01.md. Test data in bench.rs is generated by SplitMix64::next_gaussian -- real-valued. The Rust dense baseline (ionp-ion/src/baseline.rs::dense_matvec/dense_matmul) operates on real f64 throughout, matching that data honestly: a real-valued benchmark must be timed against a real-valued BLAS comparator (numpy dgemv/dgemm), never a complex one, or the baseline pays a dtype tax the algorithm being measured never asked for. Ion's own operators are typed Complex64 internally (structured-operator algebra needs it in general), and that internal cost is Ion's to carry -- it is not charged to the baseline. This file records the DECISION, not a number: there is nothing here to regenerate.

dispatch_gate._note: n=2048. Detection is a ONE-TIME cost; break-even is in applications. This is the table my earlier falsification measured exactly one row of.

unstructured.why: No structure to exploit. smart() returns a dense wrapper: never slower, never faster. THIS ROW is what GOAL-ion-array.md wrongly generalized to the whole premise.

honesty_gate.must_remain_true: On a genuinely incompressible dense matmul, no honest method beats BLAS. Measured in the reference implementation's frontier bench: Strassen-Winograd 0.71-0.93x (LOSES to Accelerate); randomized low-rank on a flat spectrum reaches 31.9x speed at 0.99 relative error, i.e. useless. 'Faster for all cases' is realised as: never slower than numpy, and faster wherever any speedup is possible.
honesty_gate.detection_must_be_subcubic: All detection tests must be O(n^2) or better. Diagonal/toeplitz/circulant are direct entry inspection; low-rank uses a randomized range finder at O(n^2 r). If detection ever becomes O(n^3) (e.g. a full SVD), break-even moves from ~8-94 applications to ~1000 and the library loses its reason to exist. This is the exact error that sank the previous attempt.

inherited_gaps._note: Open work carried forward from the reference. NOT credited as done.
inherited_gaps.composition_algebra: Only Circulant@Circulant and LowRank@LowRank collapse to closed form. All other pairs fall back to a lazy ProductOperator - cheap at matvec time, never algebraically simplified.
inherited_gaps.closed_form_scope: Closed form covers only the dephasing family (jump operators diagonal in H's eigenbasis). General non-commuting Lindbladian still needs brute-force O(n^4..n^6) - precisely the cost the closed form exists to avoid.
inherited_gaps.nika_povm_validity: born_readout() never checks the completeness relation sum_i P_i = I. Hand it an invalid projector set and it returns confident numbers.
inherited_gaps.sparse_detection: Named in detect.py's docstring, never implemented.
inherited_gaps.spectral_activations: spectral_gelu / spectral_softmax are ifft->real->fft round trips with no asymptotic win. The reference says so in-source; keep that honesty.
